title: Tensor decomposition for a finite Galois field extension
statement: Let $L$ be a field [def-pc-field-extension] and let $E/L$ be a finite Galois extension (finite and separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], normal) with group $Q=\operatorname{Aut}_L(E)$ [def-pc-field-extension]; for $q\in Q$ write $\operatorname{Spec}q:\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}E$ for the induced morphism [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. (1) The $L$-algebra map $\varphi:E\otimes_LE\to\prod_{q\in Q}E$ [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] with $\varphi(a\otimes b)=(a\,q(b))_{q\in Q}$ is an isomorphism. (2) Let $\pi:\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}L$ be induced by $L\subseteq E$, let $W=\operatorname{Spec}E\times_{\operatorname{Spec}L}\operatorname{Spec}E$ be the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] with projections $p_1,p_2:W\to\operatorname{Spec}E$, and let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of sets on the small etale site of $\operatorname{Spec}L$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets] ($\operatorname{Spec}E$ and $W$ are etale over $\operatorname{Spec}L$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $p_1,p_2$ are morphisms of the site). Then there is a bijection $\beta:\mathcal F(W)\to\prod_{q\in Q}\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}E)$ such that for every $s\in\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}E)$ one has $\beta(s|_{p_1})=(s)_{q\in Q}$ and $\beta(s|_{p_2})=\bigl((\operatorname{Spec}q)^*s\bigr)_{q\in Q}$, where $s|_{p_i}=\mathcal F(p_i)(s)$ and $(\operatorname{Spec}q)^*s=\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}q)(s)$.

source.place: Tag 03SF, finite etale objects under a finite Galois extension (the decomposition of the base change into copies indexed by the Galois group)

proof.text: Choose alpha in E with E=L(alpha) by the finite separable primitive-element lemma. Let f be the minimal polynomial of alpha over L. The quotient description for a simple algebraic extension identifies L[T]/(f) with E, sending the class of T to alpha. The quotient has L-basis 1,T,...,T^(deg f-1), so deg f=[E:L].

Write n=deg f and identify E with L[T]/(f) by Step 1, b=g(alpha) corresponding to the class of g in L[T]. Since f maps to 0 in E[T]/(f), the tensor universal property gives an L-algebra map psi: E tensor_L (L[T]/(f)) -> E[T]/(f) with psi(a tensor (g mod f)) = a g mod f. By Step 1, L[T]/(f) has L-basis 1,T,...,T^(n-1), so E tensor_L (L[T]/(f)) is a free E-module with basis 1 tensor T^i (i<n); E[T]/(f) is a free E-module with basis T^i (i<n) by division with remainder by the monic f. The E-linear map psi sends the first basis to the second, so it is an isomorphism, and a tensor b goes to a g mod f with g(alpha)=b.

source.place: tensor product universal property and base change of a polynomial quotient

proof.text: Because E/L is normal, every root of f in E is q(alpha) for an L-automorphism q by the conjugate-root lemma, and conversely every q(alpha) is a root. Separability makes these roots pairwise distinct; the finite Galois fixed-field lemma gives |Q|=[E:L]=deg f, and q is determined by q(alpha) because E=L(alpha), so these roots are exactly the |Q| elements indexed by Q. Thus f=product_{q in Q}(T-q(alpha)) in E[T].

proof.text: Apply the distinct-linear-factor Chinese-remainder isomorphism to f over E. It sends the class of a polynomial g(T) to (g(q(alpha)))_q. Combining this with the preceding tensor identification sends a tensor a tensor b to (a q(b))_q, proving that phi is an L-algebra isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 00U3, Chinese-remainder factorization into distinct linear factors

proof.text: The algebra isomorphism just proved gives the affine fibre-product decomposition and the labels of the two projections by the child affine consequence node.

The finite-separable-spectrum etale lemma makes Spec E and the finite coproduct decomposition etale over Spec L, so these are objects and morphisms of the small etale site. Apply the finite-coproduct sheaf-sections statement to the resulting open-and-closed coproduct. Its restriction bijection is beta, and the projection labels give beta(s|_{p_1})=(s)_q and beta(s|_{p_2})=((Spec q)^*s)_q.

lean.statement: theorem finiteGaloisTensorDecomposition (L E : Type u) [Field L] [Field E] [Algebra L E] [FiniteDimensional L E] [IsGalois L E] (F : Sheaf ((Spec (CommRingCat.of L)).smallEtaleTopology) (Type v)) : (∃ φ : (E ⊗[L] E) ≃ₐ[L] ((E ≃ₐ[L] E) → E), ∀ (a b : E) (q : E ≃ₐ[L] E), φ (a ⊗ₜ[L] b) q = a * q b) ∧ (let π : Spec (CommRingCat.of E) ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L) := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap L E)) ∃ (hπ : Etale π) (hW : Etale (pullback.fst π π ≫ π)), letI : Etale π := hπ letI : Etale (pullback.fst π π ≫ π) := hW let U : (Spec (CommRingCat.of L)).Etale := .mk π let V : (Spec (CommRingCat.of L)).Etale := .mk (pullback.fst π π ≫ π) ∃ (p₁ p₂ : V ⟶ U) (σ : (E ≃ₐ[L] E) → (U ⟶ U)), p₁.left = pullback.fst π π ∧ p₂.left = pullback.snd π π ∧ (∀ q : E ≃ₐ[L] E, (σ q).left = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom q.toRingEquiv.toRingHom)) ∧ ∃ β : F.obj.obj (Opposite.op V) ≃ ((E ≃ₐ[L] E) → F.obj.obj (Opposite.op U)), (∀ s q, β (F.obj.map p₁.op s) q = s) ∧ (∀ s q, β (F.obj.map p₂.op s) q = F.obj.map (σ q).op s))
